items.followUp: State the difference between an atom and a molecule, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: A compound’s elements are chemically combined in a definite proportion.
rubric.description: States that the elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed proportion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for chemical combination and fixed proportion.

rubric.why: A compound has properties different from those of its constituent elements.
rubric.description: States that a compound’s properties differ from those of its constituent elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the property distinction.

rubric.why: Mixture constituents are physically mixed and may be present in any proportion.
rubric.description: States that a mixture is formed by physical mixing in variable proportions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for physical mixing and variable proportion.

rubric.why: The substances in a mixture retain their individual properties.
rubric.description: States that mixture constituents retain their individual properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the retained-properties distinction.

rubric.why: Mixture components can be separated by physical methods, whereas the elements in a compound require chemical methods of separation.
rubric.description: States that the components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct separation method or general statement.

modelAnswer: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements are chemically combined in a fixed proportion by mass.
The properties of a compound are different from the properties of its constituent elements.
A mixture is formed when two or more substances are physically mixed in any proportion.
The substances in a mixture retain their individual properties.
The components of a mixture can be separated by physical methods; the elements of a compound can be separated only by chemical methods.

items.followUp: Write four properties of covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Many ionic compounds form crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Identifies ionic compounds as crystalline solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this property.

rubric.why: Strong electrostatic attractions between ions require considerable energy to overcome.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds have high melting points or high boiling points.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either high melting point or high boiling point.

rubric.why: Ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are generally soluble in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this solubility property.

rubric.why: Ions conduct charge when they are mobile in a melt or aqueous solution.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or dissolved in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct conditions for electrical conductivity.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are usually crystalline solids.
They have high melting and boiling points because of strong electrostatic forces between oppositely charged ions.
They are generally soluble in water.
They conduct electricity in the molten state or in aqueous solution because their ions are free to move.

items.followUp: Compare the atomic models proposed by Dalton and Thomson.

rubric.why: Rutherford proposed a small, positively charged nucleus.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford’s atom contains a small positive nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the nucleus and its positive charge.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s scattering experiment showed that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.description: States that most of the atom is empty space.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this feature of Rutherford’s model.

rubric.why: Rutherford’s theory did not explain why the atom is stable.
rubric.description: States that Rutherford’s theory failed to explain atomic stability.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this limitation of Rutherford’s theory.

rubric.why: Bohr proposed that electrons occupy fixed orbits or energy levels with definite energies.
rubric.description: States that Bohr’s electrons occupy fixed orbits or energy levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the quantised-orbit distinction.

rubric.why: In Bohr’s model, electrons absorb or emit energy when they move between energy levels.
rubric.description: States that electrons absorb or emit energy when changing energy levels.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the energy change associated with transitions between levels.

modelAnswer: Rutherford proposed that an atom has a small, positively charged nucleus at its centre, with electrons revolving around the nucleus.
Most of the atom is empty space.
Rutherford’s theory did not explain the stability of the atom.
Bohr proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in fixed orbits, or energy levels, each having a definite energy.
Electrons do not radiate energy while in a fixed orbit; they absorb or emit energy when they move between energy levels.

items.followUp: Describe diffusion in gases and state two factors that affect its rate.

rubric.why: Diffusion is the spontaneous spreading and intermixing of particles from higher to lower concentration.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion as particles spreading from a region of higher concentration to one of lower concentration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the core description and direction of diffusion.

rubric.why: Liquid particles move and intermix, but diffusion is slower in liquids than in gases because the particles are closer together.
rubric.description: Describes diffusion in liquids and notes that it is slower than in gases.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct liquid-specific description.

rubric.why: Increasing temperature increases particle motion and speeds up diffusion.
rubric.description: Names temperature as a factor and gives its effect on the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the temperature factor with its correct effect.

rubric.why: A greater concentration difference increases the rate of diffusion.
rubric.description: Names concentration difference as a factor and gives its effect on the rate of diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second factor with its correct effect.

modelAnswer: Diffusion in liquids is the spontaneous intermixing of particles as they move randomly from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
Diffusion is slower in liquids than in gases because liquid particles are closer together and experience stronger intermolecular forces.
Temperature affects diffusion: increasing temperature increases particle motion and makes diffusion faster.
Concentration difference affects diffusion: a greater concentration difference makes diffusion faster.

items.followUp: State two properties of a proton.

rubric.why: A neutron has no electrical charge.
rubric.description: States that a neutron is electrically neutral.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the charge property.

rubric.why: A neutron has a mass of approximately one atomic mass unit.
rubric.description: States that a neutron has approximately 1 amu of mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the mass property.

modelAnswer: A neutron has no electrical charge; it is electrically neutral.
Its mass is approximately 1 atomic mass unit (amu).
